assign.outcome:
**The front page shows the framework instead of describing it.** `/` graded 2/2/2 in the site audit - hero text and five link cards, no live demo, a 40em column on a 3440 screen. It grades **3/3/3** now at 400 / 1920 / 3440, with zero console errors and no horizontal overflow.

**The fold** (1000px) holds four regions, laid out by container queries on the region rather than media queries on the window (the sidebar is 19em of the difference):

- **3440** - three tracks across 2986px: the thesis, the live demo (1443px), the three latest posts (1031px), then the four section cards as a full-width row. Last pixel at 990.
- **1920** - the same three tracks at 416 / 619 / 442, section cards below. Last pixel at 920.
- **400** - stacked: thesis, the demo running, and the posts head at 976.

**The demo is `demo()` wrapping `demo.app()`** - a four-page tree, its rail, its crumb bar and its router, running in the box, with the code that built it printed above it (`fn.toString()`, so the sample IS the source). Clicking CSS inside the box walks the miniature to `/web/css/` and never touches the address bar - proved headless. Chosen over the column row, the generator and the palette because it is the thesis sentence made clickable; the Panel was out because `/framework/` already opens with it.

**The blog reads the manifest.** `blog/posts.js` is data-only with no imports, so the front lists three posts without loading a single post module. The Blog CARD is gone - the region with three real posts and an All posts link is the same link said better.
